meta.move: Skilled teacher reaches the deal, asks 'Do we have an agreement?', then sends END MEETING
meta.expect: END MEETING gets FOLLOW-UP EMAIL and DEBRIEF at once

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen gets a zero, and did anyone speak to him first?
Thanks for coming in. The school's AI checker flagged Owen's essay at 94 percent, so the zero stands.

A score from software. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student," and your procedure says the same. So what else do you have, Hale?
Let me start again. I entered the zero before I called you. Our procedure says I should have called first. That was wrong, and I'm sorry Owen found out on his phone in class.
Okay. Now show me what you have on the essay.

The checker score is the weakest thing I have, and it isn't why I'm concerned. I've turned my screen to you. This is the version history of Owen's essay. The document was created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. Then 23 minutes of font, name and spacing changes. No earlier drafts.

11:31, 11:52, 11:58, I'm writing those down. Plenty of students write somewhere else and paste it in, so a paste proves where the words landed, not who wrote them. Was Owen asked about that before you entered anything, or did you skip 4.1 too?

If he wrote it over the weekend in another document, he can show us that document and its history, and I'll look at it gladly. Second thing. The essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." Here's the play open to that scene. That line is not in Hamlet. Look for it yourself.
Give me the book. A seventeen-year-old getting a quotation wrong is a citation error, not proof of anything, so is that line anywhere else in what he handed in, or anything close to it?
Third. On October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing that Hamlet delays out of cowardice. Here's the outline. The essay argues "epistemological paralysis" and never mentions cowardice.

Students change their argument between an outline and an essay, Hale; that's what an outline is for. And you skipped my question about the quotation. Is the invented line the only problem with it, or is there more?

Fourth. On November 2 I asked Owen about his essay for five minutes. My notes written that day say that when I asked what "epistemological paralysis" means, he said "like, being stuck", and he could not say which scene his second paragraph was about.

So you did speak to him on November 2, before the zero. A kid put on the spot for five minutes freezes, so did he know that conversation was about whether he'd written it? And I'd like those notes on paper, along with an answer on the quotation and the outline.

Fifth. His in-class writing from September 24: 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, comma splices throughout, no quotations. Here it is beside the essay, which has none of those errors and nine quotations cited by act, scene and line.

Forty minutes in class against a take-home essay he could revise is not a comparison, and you still owe me answers on the quotation, the outline and that conversation. Whatever you think you have, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. What are you actually proposing, Hale?

I'm not asking you to agree he did anything. Procedure 4.4 allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. It would be private, not in front of his class. If it shows the learning, its mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing to you tonight.

That's 4.4, private and in writing, and Owen does it to put this behind him, nothing more. The rewrite happens next week and the new mark is in well before December 1, because his scholarship applications close that day. My questions about the quotation and the outline go in my email.
I know his marks matter for his applications this semester. He can write it this Thursday after school, and I'll have it marked within two days.
Okay: Thursday after school, private, marked within two days, its mark replacing the zero, nothing on his record, and all of it in writing to me tonight.
So: a private supervised rewrite this Thursday, its mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, all in writing tonight. Do we have an agreement?
Yes, once it's in my inbox tonight.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed that Owen will do a private supervised rewrite this Thursday after school, that it will be marked within two days, that its mark will replace the zero, and that nothing will go on his record. I still want your answers on the quotation, on the outline, and on whether Owen knew what your November 2 conversation was about. I expect your written confirmation of all of this tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position: she agreed to a private supervised rewrite on Thursday, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing on his record, and she still wants your written confirmation tonight and answers on her open points; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4.
What moved her: Showing the version history with its exact times, then answering her paste defence by asking for the other document, because it was dated, specific, tied to his work, and something she could check herself.
What cost ground: Opening with the checker score and saying the zero stands, because it handed her the vendor's own warning and set her back before you had shown anything.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay late on the night before it was due, close to the kind of night she was afraid of; that proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she called the invented quotation a citation error, answer it right there, for example by asking whether that line or its source appears anywhere in the play or his notes, rather than moving on to the outline and leaving her an open point for her email.
